title: fix(scripts): the polarity census reads the optional marker as a decoration, not as part of the key (objectui#9794)
body:
Fixes #9794

Clause-②: no

`keyHead` cut a backticked span at its type annotation and nowhere else, so a key mention
spelled the way a face declares the key — `allowCollapse?: boolean` — had head
`allowCollapse?`, which is not an identifier, and the whole mention was dropped. That is a
**false negative**, the opposite direction to the false positives objectui#9766 removed from
the same function, and the harder shape to notice: a false positive gets seen and complained
about, while a key mention dropped whole means that assertion was never judged at all.

## 1. The question came first, and it was answered by measuring the corpus

The card refuses to pre-answer it: **is `allowCollapse?` a legitimate spelling of a key
mention in this corpus, or should an author write the bare name?** If legitimate, strip the
marker; if not, the current behaviour is correct and the card is a docblock repair. The two
answers are opposite changes, so the corpus decides.

**Ref: `26ac503690` (`origin/main` at this branch's point), working tree clean, corpus
`.changeset/`.** Re-derive with the instrument's own exports — the probe is the card's:
a backticked span whose head, cut at `:`, ends in `?` and whose remainder is a member-key
spelling.

```js
import {
  MEMBER_KEY_SPELLING, readCorpus, segmentSentences, matchesPopulation,
} from './scripts/changeset-polarity-census.mjs';
const optional = (span) => {
  const head = span.replace(/^`/, '').replace(/`$/, '').trim().split(':')[0].trim();
  return head.endsWith('?') && MEMBER_KEY_SPELLING.test(head.slice(0, -1));
};
// leg A: every backticked span in the corpus
// leg B: only spans inside sentences `matchesPopulation` accepts, in assertion position
```

| reading at `26ac503690` | value |
| --- | --- |
| entries scanned (`.changeset/*.md`, README excluded) | 1681 |
| leg A — spans carrying the marker, whole corpus | 143, across 83 entries |
| leg B — the same spans inside sentences the census actually judges | 14, across 10 entries |
| of leg B, in assertion position / in quoted position | 14 / 0 |

Leg B is the decisive one, and it is not a tail of near-misses: every one of those fourteen
is an ordinary key mention written in declaration form — `data?: ViewData`, `value?: never`,
`actionVariant?: 'default' | 'destructive'`, `error?: string`, `disabled?:`, `series?`,
`view?` / `filter?` / `sort?` / `limit?`. Their authors were quoting a face, which is the
most precise way a changeset body can name a key. The spelling is legitimate here.

⇒ **Strip the marker.** The opposite answer would have required calling 143 mentions by 83
entries' authors an error, and the instrument does not get to make that ruling about prose it
only reads.

## 2. The rule, and why it is a rule rather than a patch

> A member key is a NAME, and the backticked span has to BE that name.

That sentence is objectui#9766's and it did not change. What changed is the list of
**decorations** a name may wear before it stops being a name: the type annotation was the
whole list, and the optional marker belongs on it beside the annotation, because both are
written by a *declaration* and neither renames the key. The marker sits before the
annotation, so it is cut after it.

⚠️ And the rule is anchored, not a blanket delete: **only a TRAILING marker is a decoration.**
In `props?.foo` the `?` is optional chaining and the span stays refused as the code fragment
it is. The corpus makes that boundary real rather than hypothetical — it writes Vite resource
specifiers as backticked spans (`?raw`, `?url`, `?inline`), and an unanchored strip
manufactures a key out of each of them. That is the pin that fails under mutation M2 below.

The rule is written into the reader's docblock and into the instrument's limits list, which
the header itself asks to be extended when another source is found. ⛔ No count from the
measurement above is written into the tree (commandment #9): the header names the probe and
points here for the reading and its ref.

## 3. What changed

- `scripts/changeset-polarity-census.mjs` — `keyHead` cuts the trailing marker after the
  annotation; its rule docblock (point 1) now names both decorations and the trailing anchor;
  the limits list gains the optional-marker entry with its residue.
- `scripts/__tests__/changeset-polarity-census.test.ts` — five pins, described below.

## 4. Every new pin shown FAILING, with the restore proven

Each mutation: exactly one textual replacement asserted to occur once, the injected and the
removed text counted on disk before and after, the mutated blob hash shown to differ from the
`HEAD` blob, the suite run, then `git checkout HEAD -- FILE` and the restore **proven** by
blob-hash equality plus an empty `git diff HEAD`. There is no build step between the mutation
and the run: the test imports the `.mjs` directly, so the bytes under test are the bytes on
disk. Mutations ran against `HEAD` blob `595cb1a5a6ac3b43d76683a0f531221e38e4db2c`.

| mutation | what it breaks | pins that went RED | suite |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **M1** — drop the marker cut (back to the pre-repair reader) | the repair itself | "reads the key out of a declaration spelling", "the marker does not smuggle a language word past the tree gate", "ONE reading, so keys and their polarity land on the same head" | 3 failed / 40 passed |
| **M2** — unanchor the cut (`/\?$/` → `/\?/g`) | the trailing anchor | "DARK LEG — only a TRAILING marker is a decoration" | 1 failed / 42 passed |
| **M3** — disable cross-sentence pronoun resolution | the blindness fixture | "⛔ did NOT buy the recovered mentions with blindness", plus the four objectui#9727 pins it restates | 5 failed / 38 passed |

Restore after every one of the three: blob back to `595cb1a5a6ac3b43d76683a0f531221e38e4db2c`,
`git diff HEAD` empty. Unmutated, the file is green: `Test Files 1 passed (1) · Tests 43
passed (43)`.

M3 is there because a pin that only restates another card's assertion can rot into a comment;
running it red proves it is still wired to the mechanism it claims to guard.

## 5. Traded nothing away — the pinned blindness fixture, before and after

The instrument carries objectui#9727's motivating site by its **pre-repair text**. Reading it
with the pre-repair reader (`scripts/changeset-polarity-census.mjs` checked out at
`26ac503690`, restore proven the same way) and with this branch's reader (`e6923ab9ce`):

| `01-pronoun-pre-repair` | before (`26ac503690`) | after (`e6923ab9ce`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| keys flagged | `allowCollapse`, `cardTitle`, `columns`, `titleField` | identical |
| every flag reached across a sentence boundary | true | true |
| every flag negative, on `ObjectKanbanSchema` | true | true |
| fixture-corpus totals (contradictions / matched assertions / pronoun-resolved) | 10 / 11 / 1 | 10 / 11 / 1 |

Exactly the four keys objectui#9713 adjudicated, every one reached across a sentence
boundary. Three would have meant the instrument was broken, not sharpened.

## 6. The census reading, before and after, and what moved

Both readings are `node scripts/changeset-polarity-census.mjs --json` over the **same corpus
bytes** — this branch's diff touches two files under `scripts/`, so `.changeset/` is identical
at both refs. Controls PASS on both runs.

| reading | before (`26ac503690`) | after (`e6923ab9ce`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| entries / sentences scanned | 1681 / 18128 | 1681 / 18128 |
| matched assertions / entries | 221 / 177 | 221 / 177 |
| candidate contradictions | **119 across 56 entries** | **121 across 58 entries** |
| claims naming a schema this tree does not declare | 61 | 61 |

⭐ The count RISES, which is what repairing a false negative does, and it is not a regression.
But the number alone would be a lie about what happened, so here is the whole movement:
**three flags in, one out, net +2.** Newly read key mentions, measured the same way (the
pre-repair reader replicated beside the repaired one over the matched assertion sentences):
**8 mentions recovered across 5 sentences in 5 entries** — `data`, `series`, `actionVariant`,
`error`, and `view` / `filter` / `sort` / `limit` in one sentence.

- **IN — `7744-chart-type-internal-only.md`, `ChartDataSeriesSchema.series`, positive.** The
  honest one: `series?` was dropped whole before and is now read. The flag itself is a
  **WINDOW PAIRING** candidate, the instrument's own largest named limit — the sentence
  predicates `series?` of `ChartRenderer`'s union and names the authoring schema in a
  different clause. A candidate, not a defect, exactly as the header says.
- **IN — `6951-tree-view-data-retired.md`, `TreeViewSchema.data`, negative.**
- **IN, and the one OUT — `6951-text-value-retired.md`: `TextSchema.value` negative arrives,
  `BaseSchema.value` positive leaves.** These two are the same mechanism and they are *not* a
  new key: both sentences already yielded the key from a bare mention. What moved is the
  **polarity**. The newly read span (`value?: never`, `data?: never`) is now the *first*
  occurrence of that head, so per-key polarity resolves in the clause that span sits in — and
  that clause's text contains the word `never`, which the clause negator test reads as a
  negation. The claim flips to negative, and under a negative reading the contradicted schema
  is the one that *has* the member rather than the one that lacks it — hence the swap on
  `6951-text-value-retired.md`.

⚠️ That last mechanism is a pre-existing residue of POLARITY BY CLAUSE, not something this
branch introduced: a clause whose *annotation* spells the type `never` has been readable as a
negated clause since polarity was narrowed to clauses. This repair only made those two
sentences reach it. It is out of this card's scope (⛔ objectui#9754 slice 2 and objectui#9767
are separately carded on this same file and this same pin file, and one card at a time is that
fence's whole point), so it is reported here and in the hand-back rather than fixed or
widened into.

## 7. Changeset: none, and the reason is measured rather than inherited

`node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` on this branch, exit 0:

> Compared the working tree with 26ac50369 (merge-base with origin/main): 2 file(s) changed,
> 0 of them published source of a package the release covers, 0 of them a manifest whose
> published contract moved, 0 under a package changesets ignores, 0 changeset(s) added.
> ✅ No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no
> changeset is owed.

Both files live under `scripts/`; nothing published moves. ⛔ objectui#9766's choice is not
treated as a precedent in either direction — it is not followed *because* it was made, and it
is not broken to prove independence. The gate says none is owed, so none is written, and the
unsettled question objectui#9795 carries (a changeset written about this instrument becomes
this instrument's own input) simply does not arise on this branch. If objectui#9795 later
rules that an empty-frontmatter declaration is owed even here, that ruling lands on its own
card, not as a silent habit started by this one.

## 8. Gates run locally

Exit codes captured to a file **before** any pipe (`cmd > out 2>&1; EXIT=$?`), never read
through `| head`/`| tail`.

- `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/changeset-polarity-census.test.ts` — 0 ·
  `Test Files 1 passed (1) · Tests 43 passed (43)`
- `pnpm -s run type-check:scripts` — 0
- `pnpm -s run check:control-bytes` — 0 · plus a direct scan of both changed files for
  control bytes: no hits
- `pnpm -s run check:new-line-citations` — 0
- `pnpm -s run check:entry-guard` — 0
- `pnpm -s run check:test-path-roots` — 0
- `pnpm -s run check:changeset-claims` — 0
- `pnpm -s run check:pending-changeset-literals` — 0
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` — 0
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over both changed paths — 0,
  `NOT GOVERNED`

**Lint was narrowed, and the narrowing is measured rather than assumed.** The repo-wide
population is `pnpm lint:root` (`eslint .` with the package/example/app/docs ignore patterns),
which is CI's run. Locally: `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the two
changed files — exit 0, and the JSON carries **2** file results, 0 errors and 0 warnings.
The narrowing excludes nothing because **type-aware linting is not enabled in this tree**
(`eslint.config.js` sets no `project` and no `projectService`), so no lint verdict on an
untouched file can move as a result of this diff. The tree-wide run stays CI's.

## 9. Acceptance notes

Out of scope, seen and deliberately **not** widened into, ⛔ and no card filed from this seat:

- **A type annotation spelling `never` makes its declaration clause read NEGATIVE.** Detailed
  in section 6. Pre-existing, POLARITY BY CLAUSE's territory (objectui#9754 slice 2), and the
  serial fence over this file forbids carrying it here. Dedupe words: `never as clause
  negator` · `polarity by clause` · `annotation text read as prose` · `changeset polarity
  census` · `retirementTombstone sentence`.
- Noted, not filed: the instrument's limits list is now long enough that a reader meets five
  named sources before the first line of code. No defect, no assertion at risk; whoever next
  restructures this header will meet it.
